title: He was dead.
paragraphs:
He was dead.
But not inactive.

Three days of silence.
No sermons. No miracles. No crowds.
And heaven… said nothing.
So what was Jesus doing?
Was He just… waiting?

Here’s the tension we feel:
The cross looked like defeat.
The tomb looked like the end.

Even His followers scattered.
Hope buried with Him.
But here’s what we miss…
God does His deepest work in the places that look the most silent.
Scripture pulls back the curtain—just enough.
In 1 Peter 3:18–20, it says Jesus was “made alive in the spirit” and went to proclaim to the spirits in prison.
Some scholars interpret this as Jesus declaring His victory over fallen spiritual powers.
In Ephesians 4:9, it says He “descended to the lower earthly regions.”
And in Matthew 12:40, Jesus Himself said He would be “three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.”
So what was happening?
Not inactivity.
Victory in the unseen.

While the world thought it was over…
Jesus was confronting death at its root.

Not negotiating.
Not struggling.
Conquering.

Sin thought it won.
Hell thought it held Him.
The grave thought it sealed Him.
But Colossians 2:15 says He “disarmed the powers and authorities… triumphing over them by the cross.”
Let that sink in.

The silence of Saturday was not weakness.
It was war.
And here’s why this matters for you.
Because some of you are living in that “third day tension.”

Prayers unanswered.
Situations unmoved.
God feels… quiet.
But don’t mistake silence for absence.
Jesus is working in places you cannot see.

In your hidden battles.
In your buried pain.
In the graveyards of your past.
And then—
Sunday came.

The stone rolled.
The grave lost.
Death bowed.

And the same Jesus who stepped out of that tomb…
is still rewriting stories today.

So if you feel stuck in between—
between promise and breakthrough,
between prayer and answer—
Don’t quit on Day Two.
Resurrection is already in motion.
Turn to Him.

Repent.
Trust the finished work of the cross.
Receive the life only Jesus gives.
Because those three days weren’t empty.

They were filled with the power
that now saves you.
Someone you love is living in their “silent Saturday.”
“We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.”
